purpose: point-in-time scorecard of external forecasts against the first publication of the fact on the frozen protocol windows W1/W2: who is more accurate, when, and with what coverage

publication_policy.note: even when the licence register would allow publishing a sample (NY Fed), the committed report keeps third-party forecast/actual values outside git; only aggregates, counts, metadata and hashes are written

protocol.actuals_rule: Both are always reported, never pooled. T3 uses the NBER chronology as of the evaluation date for both; its secondary actuals equal its primary actuals.

losses.rule: Every criterion that uses a loss must hold for each loss applicable to the pair; the loss is never chosen after seeing results.

pit_rules.publication_date: a forecast is usable only if its publication date is on or before the origin (origin_policy.default); for the SPF the date is the official news release
pit_rules.no_lookahead: publication_date > origin -> LOOKAHEAD_REJECTED (or the source-specific reason)
pit_rules.actuals: primary actual = first publication from the ALFRED vintage archive; a point whose first-publication vintage is at or before the origin is rejected
pit_rules.windows: an origin belongs to a window only if the origin and the target period are inside it
pit_rules.covid_exclusion: Origins whose target period lies in 2020-03 to 2021-02 are excluded from W2 and reported separately; for T3 this covers origins whose interval (t, t+h] contains those months.
pit_rules.quantiles: a distribution is scored only on the protocol 5-95% grid with non-crossing quantiles

metric_definitions.rmse: protocol losses.point: root mean squared error of (forecast - first publication)
metric_definitions.mae: mean absolute error, reported as context next to RMSE
metric_definitions.bias: mean signed error (forecast - actual); positive means the source over-predicts
metric_definitions.crps: protocol forecast_product.crps: twice the mean pinball loss over the 19 quantiles (5%..95% in 5% steps); requires a predictive distribution, never imputed
metric_definitions.brier: protocol losses.event: mean squared error of a probability forecast of a binary event
metric_definitions.coverage_share: scored points divided by the origins eligible in the window: how much of the window the source actually covers, not how accurate it is
metric_definitions.coverage_90: share of facts inside the source's 5-95% interval (only with a distribution)
metric_definitions.secondary: protocol actuals.secondary: the loss against the value in the vintage 12 months after the period; reported separately, never pooled with the primary actual

criteria.source: docs/173 P0-1 MVP asks for >=3 scorable sources; docs/207 M2 asks for >=2

gaps: only 2 of 4 catalogue sources could be scored; docs/207 M2 (>=2) is met, docs/173 MVP asks for >=3
project's own baselines are not joined to these origins yet ('external vs ours' is open)
CRPS and Brier are NOT_AVAILABLE for every scored source (point-only, no event probability)
limitations: MVP scope: T2_GDP_GROWTH at h=0 and h=1 only; T1/T3 and h=2/h=4 are not scored yet
the SPF file is the latest revision of the medians, not a point-in-time vintage snapshot: the release date fixes availability, errata after the survey are not audited

NY Fed Staff Nowcast is a values-only archive: 2002Q1-2015Q4 are historical reconstructions (excluded from real-time scoring) and only 2016Q1-2021Q3 rows are as published; the archive has no underlying series, so no re-estimation is possible
SPF forecasts are point (median) forecasts: CRPS and interval coverage are NOT_AVAILABLE for that source, and no distribution is imputed to make a number appear
no external source in this MVP publishes a probability for a protocol event, so Brier is implemented and tested but NOT_AVAILABLE for every scored source
GDPNow is RESTRICTED and is not used; its model quantity is represented by the project's own OPEN OWN_NOWCAST_BRIDGE, which is a different object and is not a like-for-like substitute
the scorecard contains external forecasts only: joining the project's own baselines is a separate step (docs/173 'external vs ours'), not part of this report
origins inside one quarter overlap (h=0 uses every month end), so the effective number of independent observations is smaller than the scored point count; no significance test is reported here
next_steps: add the project's own OPEN baselines (C6 forward-registry rows, R3 ensemble) to the same origins to produce the 'external vs ours' table

seek at least one more OPEN source with a matching T2 horizon mapping: GDPNow is RESTRICTED in the licence register (owner decision needed before any use) and Cleveland publishes a current-month CPI nowcast with no protocol T2 horizon mapping
extend to h=2/h=4 and to T1 once a source with a matching horizon mapping is registered
turn the report into the UC-44 subscription artifact: per-source error tables, charts and a stable API payload once >=3 sources are scored
